beats.narration_text: Namaste. I'm Priyesh Modi. This voice is synthetic, reading a script I wrote. This is the pitch for my final project. Almost none of it is built yet, and I'll say exactly which part is.

beats.narration_text: Four terms. A snapshot: a frozen, dated copy of one version's docs. A citation: the exact sentence an answer quotes, and where it's from. A refusal: saying the docs don't cover it, instead of guessing. An eval set: questions with known answers, used to score the agent.

beats.narration_text: In one sentence: it's an agent that answers coding questions from a library's official docs, pinned to the exact version you're using, and checks its own answers. Every answer will quote the section it came from. When the docs don't cover a question, it will refuse.

beats.narration_text: When it's done, it will be a public GitHub repository with a command-line agent, a snapshot loader for any docs repo at a version tag, a citation checker, and an eval log. Pydantic is the first library I'll test it on.

beats.narration_text: Why care? Coding assistants answer from training data that can be a version behind. In Pydantic, version two's migration guide renames the method that turns a model into a dictionary to model dump. An assistant can hand you the old name, and sound just as sure.

beats.narration_text: I compared two alternatives, GitHub Copilot and Cursor. Both answer fast, inside the editor, but neither told me which version an answer was for, or quoted the official docs. Mine will answer, quote, and check itself, for a version you name.

beats.narration_text: Here's how it will work. It reads your version from your requirements file, pulls the matching sections from that version's snapshot, and answers only from those.

beats.narration_text: Then a check that doesn't trust the model. Every quote has to appear, word for word, in the section it cites. If it doesn't, the answer fails.

beats.narration_text: And if the answer includes code, it will run that code in a fresh environment with only your version installed. An error or a deprecation warning means the answer was wrong, with no judgment call needed.

beats.narration_text: If nothing in the snapshot matches well enough, the agent stops and says so. A refusal can be the right answer, and the eval will score it that way.

beats.narration_text: What would it prove about me, for roles building with language models? Four things this course teaches: source grounding, a prompt contract, verification, and evaluation. The evidence will be the dated eval log and that table, not my word.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? Mostly to learn: evaluation sets, agent loops, and prompt contracts are new to me. What I already have is Python, FastAPI, Streamlit, Supabase, and C-I C-D. My cloud course web app has a GitHub Actions pipeline that runs its tests on every pull request.
